attributes.relocation_evidence: Both raw objects have .rodata size 0x1B. exception::what is 3/3 instructions, with identical words 3c600000 38630000 4e800020 in all four observations. Its .rela.text entries at object text offsets 0x6E and 0x72 are relocation types 6 and 4 through @14, addend 0. Before fix_nmw, @14 st_value is 0 and the resolved string is exception for the untouched raw object and MODIFIED! for the modified raw object. After fix_nmw, .rodata is 0x30, @14 st_value is 0x20, and both relocations resolve to exception in both objects. The intended modification is erased while instruction bytes remain unchanged.

subject: function:what__Q23std9exceptionCFv
value: Confirmed modifiability defect in the existing tools/fix_exception_objects.py fix_nmw path, separate from WebFrank. Changing only std::exception::what's return literal from exception to same-length MODIFIED! in a full-TU scratch copy compiles to the intended new string. fix_nmw silently overwrites that datum back to exception and produces an entire object identical to the fixed untouched baseline. This is a live relocated value, not merely dead padding or target-independent metadata. No production source, object, build configuration, compiler binary, or fixup behavior was changed by the experiment.
